Definition: to be transparent or clean (phys. or morally)
BiblicalUsage: zâkak means to be transparent or clean (physically or morally). In Job 9:30 we read, "If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean;". It appears again in Job 15:15: "Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight."
TheologicalSignificance: zakak is to be transparent or clean (physically or morally), and my conviction is that even the rarest words in the Bible were put there on purpose.
